selected.claim: In the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, 50 of 193 planned experiments were completed; across 112 comparable positive/null effects with numerical values, 51 (46%) met at least three of five binary replication-success criteria.
selected.boundary: Selected high-impact preclinical cancer-biology sample only; not a universal reproducibility rate, scientific truth, or evidence that decentralized infrastructure improves replication.

source.title: Investigating the replicability of preclinical cancer biology

selected.claim: Scientific digital objects benefit from machine-actionable findability, accessibility, interoperability and reusability requirements with persistent identifiers and rich metadata.
selected.boundary: FAIR governs stewardship and reuse properties; it does not establish scientific truth, statistical validity, clinical validity, or superiority of decentralized infrastructure.

source.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship

research_library.claim: Improving research reliability requires interventions across methods, reporting, dissemination, reproducibility, evaluation and incentives.
research_library.boundary: Motivates reproducibility controls; does not validate a DeSci protocol or prove decentralization improves scientific outcomes.

research_library.source_title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
research_library.claim: Reproducible computational research requires tracking result production, exact software versions, version-controlled scripts, intermediate results, random seeds, raw data and links from statements to results.
research_library.boundary: Rules and practices, not proof that a specific implementation is scientifically valid or reproducible.

research_library.claim: Scientific software development benefits from explicit practices for data management, code design, collaboration, testing and reproducibility.
research_library.boundary: Recommended practices; no client-outcome evidence and no requirement for decentralization.

research_library.source_title: The Open Provenance Model core specification (v1.1)
research_library.claim: A technology-agnostic provenance model can represent and exchange provenance across systems and support valid provenance inferences.
research_library.boundary: A provenance graph records lineage; graph structure alone does not prove correctness, quality or scientific truth.

research_library.source_title: Introducing the FAIR Principles for research software
research_library.claim: Research software FAIRness includes persistent/versioned identifiers, rich metadata, standardized access, licensing, provenance and interoperability.
research_library.boundary: Community-endorsed principles; satisfying them does not prove reproducibility, correctness or scientific validity.

research_library.source_title: Good enough practices in scientific computing
research_library.claim: Accessible research-computing practices include organized data, documented workflows, project organization, versioning, collaboration and citable artefacts.
research_library.boundary: Supports maintainability and reproducibility practices; not a performance benchmark and does not imply decentralization.

research_library.source_title: Towards FAIR principles for research software
research_library.claim: FAIR concepts require software-specific interpretation because software is executable, composite, evolving and versioned.
research_library.boundary: Frames FAIR-for-software requirements; not evidence that a given protocol satisfies them.

research_library.source_title: Ten simple rules for writing and sharing computational analyses in Jupyter Notebooks
research_library.claim: Reproducible notebook analyses require machine-readable environment/dependency descriptions and human-readable documentation linking code, results and narrative.
research_library.boundary: Documentation improves inspectability but does not ensure scientific validity or independent reproduction.

research_library.claim: RO-Crate provides a lightweight machine-readable package for research artefacts, identifiers, provenance, relations and annotations using JSON-LD and Schema.org.
research_library.boundary: Supports packaging and metadata exchange; does not verify computation correctness or scientific truth.

context_library.claim: EHDS-scope EHR systems are subject to applicable implementation/testing/documentation requirements.
context_library.boundary: EHDS-scope regulatory implementation context; not a measured performance gain and not automatically applicable to unrelated research software.

context_library.claim: Good-AI-practice guidance for medicines emphasizes provenance, risk-based validation, human-AI interaction and lifecycle monitoring.
context_library.boundary: Normative context; no clinical effectiveness, commercial outcome or universal regulatory-scope inference.

context_library.claim: Public professional/education record supports pharmaceutical-science training context.
context_library.boundary: Capability context only; not a DeSci certification or client result.

context_library.claim: Public professional record supports hospital radiopharmacy quality-control context.
context_library.boundary: Capability context only; not proof of DeSci client outcome.
